title: The Dry Stone
passages:
Márk broke the surface again, his mouth opening on a sound that was not a breath, and the current snatched him under before Ilka could reach him. She lunged forward, her knee cracking against the wet stone, and plunged her arm into the black water. Her fingers closed on his wrist—cold, the thread there silent—and she hauled. Ákos threw himself flat behind her, bracing his shoulders against the column, and pulled on her belt. Márk’s body dragged up the step, slick and heavy, his head lolling. He did not cough. He did not inhale. Water ran from his mouth in thin streams, and his chest stayed still.

Ilka laid her palm over his heart and felt nothing. “He’s gone,” she said, and felt no pull on her wrist. Ákos, his name still inked beside Márk’s on the ledger, spoke without flinching. “Not yet.” He pressed his mouth to Márk’s, forcing air into lungs that had been paid to the river. Ilka watched Ákos’s cheeks hollow, waited for the sting, for a memory to slip away, but the cord stayed slack. The toll was shared. The water rose another finger’s width, creeping up the step’s riser.

Márk coughed then, a wet racking sound, and turned his head to spit black water onto the stone. His eyes opened, gray and unfocused. “The step,” he said, his voice a scrap. “It’s going under.”

The ledger dripped onto Ákos’s boot. Sára’s dead hand rested on the page, fingers curled around the next blank space.
